results.title: Infrapolitics and Mobilizations: A Response by James C. Scott

raw_affiliation_strings: James C. Scott is the Sterling Professor of Politica l Scienc e an d Professo r of Anthrop olog y at Yale University. His research concerns political economy, comparative agrarian societies, theories of hegemony and resistance, peasant politics, revolution, Southeast Asia, theories o f class relations and anarchism. He is currently teaching Agrarian Studies and Rebellion, Resistance and Repression. His recent publications include Domination and the Arts o f Resistance : Hidden Transcripts (Yale UP, 1990), Seeing Like a State: How Certain Schemes to Improve the Human Condition Have Failed (Yale UP, 1997), The Art of Not Being Governed: An Anarchist History of Upland Southeast Asia (Yale UP, 2009) and, most recently, Two Cheers for Anarchism (Princeton UP, 2012). His work is translated in many languages. He is a mediocre farmer and sheep breeder in Connecticut

raw_affiliation_strings: Guillaume Marche is an Associate Professor of American studies at Université Paris-Est Créteil (France) specializing in contemporary social movements. His research focuses on sexual identities, subjectivity, and the interplay between the cultural and political—as well as the symbolical and instrumental—dimensions of collective mobilization. He is currently working on the use of LGBT biographies and memoirs in social movement sociology, and on infrapolitical forms of mobilization in San Francisco.
